questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose SFU because it is located on the unseeded Indigenous territories of the Musqueam Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh, and Kwikwetlem nations. I wanted to study Indigenous literature and gain a further understanding of the relationship between Canadian settlers and the Indigenous peoples.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was fairly easy to find the information on the SFU canvas course called exchange 101. However, it was a lot of work and stress that due to the overlapping semesters was very stress-full.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, everything was electronic due to the pandemic. The residence and housing staff mostly helped me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: this question seems to be missing something ?

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No cooking facilities were offered in the building I resided in, and the meal-plan was required.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It makes the exchange-experience easier. The students are generally a lot younger that Danish university students. Drinking and partying is not allowed in most places. The location of the campus (on burnaby mountain) has a beautiful view and surroundings such as hiking trail, and overview of Vancouver and mountains in every direction. However it is also minimum 45 minutes of public transport from most things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the campus housing is very dirty and the students do not treat it very well. The showers and bathrooms are generally quite disgusting.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose 8 courses that you want and then they check if you are eligible to take these classes. May classes has perquisites that makes it impossible to gain access to them if you are not a student at SFU.  It was difficult to understand. Most of the course I applied for was not possible for me. However the staff was very helpful and suggested courses that matched my interests and it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The SFU study aboard team lead by Eshani was available for correspondence via email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 2 out of the three classes i took were on my initial list of classes that i applied for and the last one was suggested to me by a study aboard employee and i ended up being very happy with it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep and open mind and don't be discouraged if the courses you want are not available to you. You can often find several courses that cover the same kind of topic. Be clear and firm in your correspondence if you need help in finding another course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was on the last semester of my BA and I took level 200 and 300 courses. The course material , workload and lectures seemed to be on the same level as I experience in my home-institution however my own academic level seemed to be a bit higher than most of my peers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching  was very similar, however SFU had a bigger emphasis on providing and encouraging a creative approach to assignments. Their way grading and monitoring attendance is different from UCPH and created a quite stress-full studying environment.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ENGL360 Indigenous Literature 
ENGL355 Black Canadian Literature
GSWS 230 'The Angry Woman' in Contemporary Media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of the above.
Studying Indigenous literature provide an extensive knowledge about the the complicated and horrific history of the stolen and exploited indigenous land that we know as Canada. It furthermore is a class in which you can feel and learn about this conflict by interacting with your peers. Sophy McCall is a very good professor. 

Studying Black Canadian Literature with David Chiriandy has been an absolute privilege and I would recommended it to anyone who is even slightly interested in Black literature, diaspora and the transatlantic experience.

In my gender studies class i learned feminist theory that is applicable in my everyday relations. We furthermore looked deeply on the intersectionality of feminism.

questions.answer: I don't know

questions.answer: skiing, hiking, sailing.

questions.answer: Vancouver island, ski resorts, Lynn creek valley, whale-tours ect

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy when living on campus

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Smile at them and don't be scared to ask people if they want to hang. Canadians are quite welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The drinking and frat culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature!!!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Its is going to be so much more expensive that you think save up and enjoy!!
You will be academically on a higher level that what you are at home, so do not stress. 
Soak it up it goes by so fast!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: if possible do 2 semesters ! one was too little for me. Right when you are settled in and you feel at home, it over...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the academic and social aspects.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Canadian drinking culture.
